author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: An optional specialty name in the page address narrows the veterinarian directory page and the machine-readable veterinarian list to the veterinarians holding that specialty. The machine-readable list is reinstated as a supported surface. No on-page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: Opening /vets.html?specialty=<name> for a specialty some veterinarians hold lists only those veterinarians, a page at a time.
The specialty match is the whole name and case-insensitive: a name differing only by letter case matches; a name that is only the beginning of a held specialty does not match.
Opening /vets.html?specialty=<name> for a specialty no veterinarian holds returns a normal page with no veterinarians listed.
Opening /vets.html with an empty or whitespace-only specialty lists every veterinarian, as though the parameter were absent.
Opening /vets.html with no specialty parameter lists every veterinarian a page at a time, unchanged from today.
When a narrowed directory runs to more than one page, pagination links preserve the specialty and each page lists only matching veterinarians.
Requesting /vets?specialty=<name> for a held specialty returns only the veterinarians holding it in machine-readable form.
Requesting /vets?specialty=<name> for a specialty no veterinarian holds returns a normal 200 response with an empty veterinarian list.
Requesting /vets with an empty, whitespace-only, or absent specialty returns every veterinarian, unchanged from today; the endpoint is a supported surface.
non_goals: Free-text search over veterinarian records (NG-9 keeps this out)
An on-page filter control, dropdown, or form; the filter is URL-only in this slice
Honoring more than one specialty in a single request
notes: NG-9 narrowed via docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md. Reinstates the JSON /vets surface withdrawn as REQ-VET-002; the REQ-VET-002 id stays withdrawn and is not reused. Matching semantics align with owner search: trim leading/trailing whitespace, then treat empty as no filter.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty filter reuses the established query-param-filter pattern already realized by owner search, on the existing `vet` feature package (system-design.md Contracts: VetController, VetRepository, Vet). No new module, integration, or architectural pattern. The one adjustment against current durable memory: this slice reinstates the machine-readable /vets route as a supported surface serving REQ-VET-003, which retires the Known-Defects row 'The machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' and adds REQ-VET-003 to the Implements columns of VetController, Vets, and VetRepository. Basis: read OwnerController.processFindForm/findByLastNameStartingWith and VetController/VetRepository directly (Read, not the IDE oracle — no MCP server on this run; grep/Read is the weaker basis).
integration_points: Filtering belongs in VetRepository as Spring Data derived query methods, mirroring OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith — NOT in-controller stream filtering. Whole-name case-insensitive, non-prefix semantics map to the derived query property path traversing the specialties association: a paged form `Page<Vet> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable)` for /vets.html and a collection form `Collection<Vet> findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String)` for /vets. `IgnoreCase` gives case-insensitive; plain equality (not StartingWith/Containing) gives whole-name non-prefix.

VetController branches on the trimmed specialty exactly like OwnerController: strip the parameter, treat null/blank as no filter and call the existing findAll(pageable) / findAll(); otherwise call the filtered query. Blank-as-absent must be decided in the controller before the repository call.
Pagination must be applied by the repository query (Page<Vet> over the filtered set) so getTotalPages/getTotalElements reflect matches only — never filter after paging.

vetList.html pagination links must carry the specialty. Add `specialty` to the model and extend each `@{'/vets.html?page=__..__'}` link to include the specialty parameter; prefer Thymeleaf's `@{...(page=..,specialty=..)}` URL builder so escaping is handled. When specialty is absent the links must remain unchanged in effect (empty specialty == no filter).

/vets JSON: keep the Vets wrapper and @ResponseBody unchanged (its single-root-element role for content negotiation is documented in system-design.md Contracts). Only the collection populating it is filtered; a no-match yields a Vets with an empty list, serialized as HTTP 200 with an empty vet list. No serialization change is needed.

docs/system-design.md must be updated WITH the code (owned by the implementation slice / doc-sync, not pre-edited to a future state): retire the Known-Defects row for the machine-readable route and add REQ-VET-003 to the Implements columns for VetController, Vets, VetRepository. The ADR index row for 2026-08-26-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md has already been added to docs/adr/README.md in this triage.

patterns.description: canonical query-param filter: strip parameter, treat blank as broadest search, paged derived-query call, model wiring — the template for VetController
derived paged query method pattern (findByLastNameStartingWith) — the shape for findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase

risks.risk: Both VetRepository.findAll methods are @Cacheable("vets") with no eviction (Open Question #5). New filter methods added to the same cache would key on the specialty argument; harmless given no vet write path, but the caching choice must be consistent.
risks.mitigation: Annotate the new query methods @Cacheable("vets") to match the existing style (keys auto-derive from the specialty/pageable arguments), or leave them uncached — pick one and be consistent. Do not introduce a second cache name.

risks.risk: Filtering in the controller after paging would corrupt getTotalPages/getTotalElements and break pagination-link generation on the narrowed list.
risks.mitigation: Filter at the repository query so the Page is computed over matching vets only, exactly as owner search does.

risks.risk: Pagination links that hardcode only ?page lose the specialty on navigation (acceptance criterion: links preserve specialty).
risks.mitigation: Thread specialty through the model and into every link; verified by theVetListPageShouldCarrySpecialtyAcrossPagination.

notes: NG-9 narrowing confirmed via docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md; feature is in scope, no conflict. Vocabulary: use 'Specialty' and 'Veterinarian' (short form 'Vet' in code) per docs/ubiquitous-language.md. REQ-VET-002 id stays withdrawn and is not reused; the /vets surface is reinstated under REQ-VET-003. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: specialty parameter flows into Spring Data derived query findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, generating a parameterized query with the name bound as a JDBC parameter; no string concatenation, no SQL/JPA injection surface

pagination links echo the specialty via Thymeleaf URL-expression builder @{/vets.html(page=..,specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the parameter value and HTML-escapes the th:href attribute output; no reflected XSS
controller normalizes null/blank specialty before the repository call and filters at the repository so pagination totals reflect matches only; no data-integrity drift
no new dependencies introduced; no unsafe operations, deserialization, or file/network I/O added by this change

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Private method `findPaginated` does not convey the domain entity being retrieved. The OwnerController counterpart is named `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName`, which tells a cold reader both the entity and the filter dimension. `findPaginated` could be any entity; rename to `findVetsPaginated` (or `findPaginatedVets`) so the pattern symmetry is explicit.
findings.fix: Rename method from `findPaginated` to `findVetsPaginated` and update the two call sites in `showVetList` (line 48).

findings.description: The parameter order in `addPaginationModel` is (int page, Page<Vet> paginated, Model model), but the OwnerController counterpart at line 124 declares (int page, Model model, Page<Owner> paginated) — Model and Page are swapped. Both methods are private so there is no API-compatibility concern, but the reversal breaks the symmetry a reader expects when comparing the two controllers side-by-side. Grep/Read confirmed (IDE not consulted).
findings.fix: Swap the second and third parameters: change the signature to `private String addPaginationModel(int page, Model model, Page<Vet> paginated)` and update the internal usage order accordingly.

approved_aspects: VetRepository derived-query methods use the correct Spring Data IgnoreCase/whole-name semantics with no StartingWith suffix — matches the acceptance criteria for non-prefix matching
New VetRepository methods annotated @Cacheable(vets) consistent with existing findAll methods as required by the design-block
filterSpecialty helper correctly normalizes null and whitespace-only values to null, matching the blank-as-no-filter contract from the PRD
Repository-level paging ensures getTotalPages/getTotalElements reflect the filtered set — avoids the controller-after-paging antipattern flagged in design risks
vetList.html uses Thymeleaf @{...(specialty=${specialty})} URL builder correctly — null specialty is omitted from links automatically, keeping no-filter URLs clean
Format check passes clean

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theVetListPageShouldTreatBlankSpecialtyAsNoFilter tests whitespace ("   ") but not an empty string (""). PRD acceptance criterion 4 says "empty or whitespace-only specialty" — both are required. A controller that trims then checks isEmpty passes whitespace but could fail empty if the trim logic is applied differently. The empty case must have its own assertion.

theVetsJsonEndpointShouldReturnAllVetsWhenSpecialtyAbsent covers the absent-parameter case but PRD acceptance criterion 9 says "empty, whitespace-only, or absent specialty returns every veterinarian". No test exercises GET /vets?specialty= (empty string) or GET /vets with a whitespace specialty for the JSON endpoint. These are distinct code paths from the absent case and must be covered.

theVetListPageShouldCarrySpecialtyAcrossPagination has no blank line between the stub-override Arrange phase (given(...)) and the Act phase (mockMvc.perform(...)). The testing brief requires phases separated by blank lines.
findings.fix: Add one blank line between the given(...).willReturn(...) statement and the mockMvc.perform(...) call.

findings.description: The pagination-carry assertion checks containsString("specialty=radiology") against the full rendered HTML body. This passes even if the string appears in non-link content. A narrower check — for example, asserting the string appears inside an href attribute (e.g., containsString("href") along with containsString("specialty=radiology"), or an xpath/css selector on anchor elements) — would fail precisely when pagination links lose the specialty rather than passing on incidental occurrences.
findings.fix: Replace the full-body containsString check with a targeted assertion on an anchor element href, e.g. content().string(containsString("href")) and content().string(containsString("?page=2&specialty=radiology")), or use xpath("//@href", hasItem(containsString("specialty=radiology"))).

approved_aspects: All eight test names declared in the prd-entry are present and correctly spelled

The holdingSpecialty fake faithfully models the derived-query contract: equalsIgnoreCase gives case-insensitive whole-name matching, and absence of StartingWith/Containing gives the non-prefix guarantee — the fake will detect any divergence between the controller logic and the repository contract

@MockitoBean VetRepository in @WebMvcTest is consistent with the existing VetControllerTests convention; the brief explicitly permits existing mock-framework stubs to stay, and the database is a recognised system boundary for the web-layer slice
willAnswer delegation to the hand-written holdingSpecialty helper is the right hybrid pattern: the fake captures the behavioral contract while the stub provides the @WebMvcTest seam
BDD test naming (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) followed consistently across all eight new tests
Case-insensitive and non-prefix behaviors tested with realistic values (RaDiOlOgY vs radiology; rad vs radiology)
JSON endpoint tested for both match and no-match cases with correct HTTP 200 and empty-list semantics
No JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue; MockMvc result matchers are used throughout, consistent with the existing class style
